html:
A lone acacia in the Tenere desert of Niger, the only tree for hundreds of kilometres, marked on maps as a landmark for caravans, until a truck driver knocked it down in 1973.

It was the last of a group of trees from a wetter age, its roots reaching water some 35 metres down. The salt caravans between the Air and Bilma steered by it. The dead trunk was taken to the national museum in Niamey, and a metal sculpture now stands in its place. The tree shows how far the Sahara has dried, and the routes that tie Agadez to the oases.
